meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Kissing Marilyn Monroe Is Like Kissing Hitler'?
meta.ogDescription: Tony Curtis said it about Monroe, not Monroe about anyone. Documented in print from May 1960; Curtis denied it, then admitted it in 2008.

answer.label: Not Marilyn Monroe — actually Tony Curtis
answer.authorDates: 1925–2010 · American actor · Monroe’s co-star in Some Like It Hot
answer.sourceLine: The line was said about Marilyn Monroe, not by her. Tony Curtis produced it after the kissing scene he played with Monroe in Billy Wilder’s Some Like It Hot was shot, and Quote Investigator concludes he really did say it ↗ — the earliest citation it documents is a Cumberland Times film column of 22 May 1960. Curtis denied the remark for a period, then owned it in a 2008 Time interview ↗, calling it sarcasm aimed at crew who kept needling him.

source.heading: Where the line is actually documented

docMeta.dd: Tony Curtis — about Monroe, not by her
After the kissing scene was filmed for Billy Wilder’s comedy

source.excerpt: Curtis, who has no love for Miss Monroe, said after the scene was filmed that ‘kissing Marilyn was like kissing Hitler.’
trail: Quote Investigator’s 2010 investigation ↗ gathers nine dated citations and concludes that Curtis did utter the words after the kissing scene was filmed — only his reason for saying them stays unclear.

The earliest of those citations is a Cumberland Times film column of 22 May 1960; a Deseret News interview of 3 June 1960 then has Charlton Heston joking, “I’d really like to do a picture with Marilyn … even if Tony Curtis says kissing her is like kissing Hitler,” as reproduced by Quote Investigator ↗.

Curtis confirmed the line himself in a 17 October 2008 Time Q&A ↗: watching the rushes, crew members needled him about the kiss, and he snapped back with it — “I was just pissed at them bringing it up like that.”

Wikiquote files the short form under Curtis ↗ — “It’s like kissing Hitler” — sourced to Maurice Zolotow’s 1960 biography Marilyn Monroe, p. 323. Monroe’s own Wikiquote page carries no version of the line at all.
source.excerptNote: As transcribed by Quote Investigator from a Cumberland Times column rating the best screen moments of the previous year — which had just given Curtis and Monroe its best-movie-kiss award. Note the period wording: “kissing Marilyn,” not the modern full-name form.

source.rightsNote: This is a spoken remark from around 1959, first documented in print in 1960 — far too late for public domain under the pre-1931 rule, so we do not treat it as free. In practice a six-word quip is quoted as fair use, and both the speaker’s estate and the newspapers that first printed it have a claim on the text; nothing here should be read as clearing it for reuse.

author.bio: Born Bernard Schwartz in New York in 1925, Tony Curtis was one of the biggest American screen stars of the 1950s and early 1960s, with a career spanning six decades and more than a hundred films. He was Oscar-nominated for The Defiant Ones and is best remembered for Sweet Smell of Success (1957) and Billy Wilder’s Some Like It Hot (1959), the film that produced this quip. He died on 29 September 2010.

misattribution.heading: How this ends up filed under “Marilyn Monroe quotes”
misattribution.intro: This is the rare case where a famous name attracts a quote that is not merely unsourced but grammatically about her. Because her name sits inside the sentence, aggregators and social posts file it in her column — and the wording drifts as it travels.

items.why: Monroe never said this; she was its target. Her only documented response is an August 1962 Life interview in which she refuses to name the actor and says “I think that’s his problem” ↗. Her Wikiquote page carries no such line in any section.

items.who: “Kissing Marilyn Monroe is like kissing Hitler”
items.why: The period reports are shorter. The May 1960 Cumberland Times item has “kissing Marilyn was like kissing Hitler,” a July 1960 James Bacon column has simply “It’s like kissing Hitler,” and Curtis’s own 2008 Time retelling ↗ uses “Kissing Marilyn.” The full-name version is a modern tidy-up.

Quote Investigator notes a 2001 Guardian report that Curtis had since denied the remark ↗ — which is why some retellings call it apocryphal. He reversed himself in 2008, and Legends Revealed rates the story “Apparently True” ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: Tony Curtis said it, about Marilyn Monroe, around the filming of Some Like It Hot; the earliest citation Quote Investigator documents is 22 May 1960 ↗, and Curtis confirmed the words were his in 2008.

context.heading: Why the line stuck
lead: Some Like It Hot opened in March 1959 with the most photographed woman alive in it, so “what was it like to kiss Marilyn Monroe?” became the only question anyone asked Tony Curtis. His six-word answer travelled further than any performance in the picture: within a year it was being repeated in American newspapers, and by June 1960 Charlton Heston was using it as a punchline in his own interviews ↗.

Monroe heard about it. In a Life magazine interview whose cover date fell two days before her death, she declined to name the actor and said the problem was his, not hers — a reply Quote Investigator reproduces alongside the 1960 press reports. Curtis spent decades first denying the line and then explaining it, telling Time in 2008 that he snapped it at technicians who were needling him during a screening of the rushes.
detailsBody: 1960–1965, in the press: the remark is reported straight, as evidence that Curtis resented Monroe’s conduct on set. A 1965 Pittsburgh Press interview has him repeating it and adding “I didn’t like her. She was a really mean person.”
2001: a Guardian piece on Monroe notes that Curtis is widely believed to have made the comparison — and that he has since denied it.

2008: Curtis tells Time he did say it, in irritation at crew members needling him after the rushes, and elsewhere that Monroe “was amazing to kiss” and he “was making a joke.” Quote Investigator lays the versions side by side and declines to pick a motive.
context.pull: “Well, I think that’s his problem.” — Marilyn Monroe, Life, 3 August 1962

sourcesVerified.claim: Quote Investigator concludes Tony Curtis did say kissing Marilyn was like kissing Hitler after the Some Like It Hot kissing scene was filmed, and its earliest listed citation is the Cumberland Times of 22 May 1960 (p. 26, col. 3), followed by Deseret News 3 June 1960 (Charlton Heston), Idaho State Journal 15 July 1960, Life 3 August 1962 (Monroe's reply), Pittsburgh Press 29 October 1965, and a 2001 Guardian report of Curtis's denial.

In an October 17, 2008 Time Q&A by Gilbert Cruz, Tony Curtis says that while the rushes were being screened the men present needled him about the kiss and he replied 'Kissing Marilyn was like kissing Hitler', adding 'I was just pissed at them bringing it up like that.'

Wikiquote's Tony Curtis page lists 'It's like kissing Hitler.' as his, on kissing Marilyn Monroe during the filming of Some Like It Hot (1959), sourced to Maurice Zolotow, Marilyn Monroe (1960), p. 323.
Wikiquote's Marilyn Monroe page contains no occurrence of 'Hitler' in any section, sourced, disputed or misattributed (verified by full-text search of the page source).

Legends Revealed's entertainment fact-check rates the story that Tony Curtis said kissing Marilyn Monroe was like kissing Hitler as 'Apparently True', noting he initially denied it and later admitted he had said it as a joke.
Some Like It Hot is a 1959 American comedy produced, co-written and directed by Billy Wilder, starring Marilyn Monroe, Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon, released in the US on 19 March 1959.

Tony Curtis was born Bernard Schwartz on 3 June 1925 and died 29 September 2010; American actor, career of six decades and over 100 films, Oscar-nominated for The Defiant Ones, films include Sweet Smell of Success (1957) and Some Like It Hot (1959).
